selection_rule: Spike 4 corpus selection rule (written before any file was downloaded or opened). ELIGIBLE iff, judged from the URL host and the search engine's title/description only: (E1) a direct public PDF URL, no login; (E2) published as a sample / specimen / example / how-to-read guide / demo statement, with placeholder or plainly fictional holder (e.g. MARY M MEMBER, Max Mustermann, ABC Company, John Doe, COMPANY NAME, YOUR NAME HERE); (E3) NOT from a document-sharing upload site (scribd, studocu, collegesidekick, pdfcoffee, slideshare), NOT from a statement-converter / extraction-vendor site, and NOT a real person's or real organisation's own statement (organisation transparency uploads and uploaded customer statements are excluded, the same 'reads like a real customer' rule spike 3 applied); (E4) the country has a layout profile in tests/pdfspike_layout.PROFILES; (E7) the document is primarily a statement (a how-to-read insert around a sample statement counts; a long manual with a statement appendix does not). No filter on 'has printed balances', layout difficulty, or page count beyond E7. AFTER download, automatic checks that do not print text: (E5) sha256 not in tests/fixtures/pdfspike/manifest-real.json and not a duplicate of another candidate; (E6) pdfplumber finds >= 1 character on some page (text layer present). SPLIT (deterministic, decided before download): within each country, candidates are ordered by sha256(url); HELD-OUT = the first eligible candidate of every country (7 countries) + the second eligible US candidate (the largest pool) = 8; TUNE = round-robin over countries (largest remaining pool first, ties alphabetical) taking the next eligible candidate in hash order until 8 TUNE files. A candidate failing E5/E6 is skipped and the next one in the same country's hash order takes its slot. The resulting manifest (ids, set, country, sha256, bytes, pages) is committed before any extraction.
